Assume \(n\) is a positive integer. Let \(z=e^{i\theta}\), so that \(dz=iz\,d\theta\) and \(e^{in\theta}=z^n\). The unit circle is traversed counterclockwise once.

Then
\[
e^{i\theta}\,d\theta=\frac{dz}{i},
\]
so the integral becomes
\[
I=\int_0^{2\pi} e^{i\theta} e^{-i e^{in\theta}}\,d\theta
=\frac{1}{i}\oint_{|z|=1} e^{-i z^n}\,dz.
\]

For \(n\ge 1\), the function
\[
f(z)=e^{-i z^n}
\]
is entire. Hence by Cauchy’s theorem,
\[
\oint_{|z|=1} e^{-i z^n}\,dz=0.
\]

Therefore,
\[
I=0.
\]

\[
\boxed{0}
\]
